text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Britain's leading blue chip index defied expectations of a bloody Monday and ended with only moderate losses as bargain hunting emerged in the wake of Friday's steep drop, dealers and strategists said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4835.0, down 30.8 points, or 0.63 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch shares ended up 2.6 percent, crossing back through the 900 point mark, as the return of some investors sparked technical buying, dealers said. The AEX index closed at 917.48, up 23.06 points, or 2.58 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares end off their bottom levels as Wall Street opens firmer, but local stocks still finish much weaker after their earlier hit by the Dow's nearly 250 point plunge on Friday, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7361.3, down 78.5 points, or 1.06 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1016.4, down 5.8 points, or 0.57 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9049.0, down 71.9 points, or 0.79 percent.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market slowly moved away from its early lows to close 1.8 percent down as investors nervously awaited the next U.S. session after Friday's 3.1 percent dive on Wall Street. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2618.5, down 47.7 points, or 1.79 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed lower, as the Dow Industrials' plunge on Friday hammered local shares, particularly those in the high-technology sector, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19041.10, down 284.93 points, or 1.47 percent.

FRANKFURT - The German DAX index played catch-up to Friday's severe losses on Wall Street and tumbled about four percent in early bourse trade, but pared losses over the session to end well off early lows. The DAX-30 index closed at 4078.60, down 74.26 points, or 1.79 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4080.55, up 2.96 points, or 0.07 percent.

PARIS - French shares closed 1.77 percent down after having lost over 3.3 percent earlier in the day on the back of a big slide on Wall Street on Friday when Paris was closed. The CAC-40 index closed at 2870.13, down 51.71 points, or 1.77 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index posted its biggest decline in two months on Friday, closing down 400.83 points, or 2.43 percent, at 16,096.88 as a rise in overnight rates fuelled concerns about the Hong Kong dollar. The Hang Seng index closed at 16096.88, down 400.83 points, or 2.43 percent.

MILAN - Italian stocks closed lower, falling almost two percent but with smaller losses than feared after U.S. shares began little changed following Friday's tumble. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 14125, down 280 points, or 1.94 percent.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended lower, but above early losses of some three percent, as the consolidation that marked the last six sessions continued, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5405.6, down 92.9 points, or 1.69 percent.
